slides.title: “I’m sorry, *but…”*
slides.sub: Listen to what comes after the comma.

slides.title: The "but" cancels it.
slides.body: Whatever came before it, the other person hears what comes after. That's usually the defense.

slides.title: Now it's an argument.
slides.body: "I'm sorry, but you were yelling too" asks them to apologize back. The conversation starts over.

slides.title: Two talks, not one.
slides.body: Your side of it matters. It can wait for its own conversation, after the apology has landed.

slides.title: Stop at the period.
slides.body: "I'm sorry I snapped at you." Then stop. Notice what you want to add, and what it's protecting.
